newsitem.title: USA: Evergreen to sell 3 radio stations.
newsitem.headline: Evergreen to sell 3 radio stations.

text.p: Evergreen Media Corp. said Tuesday it agreed to sell three of its radio stations to Douglas Broadcasting/Personal Achievement Radio for $18 million.
The stations are WZHF-AM and WBZS-AM in Washington DC, and KDFC-AM San Francisco.
The deal is scheduled to close in the third quarter, subject to approval by the Federal Communications Commission.

The deal is part of a divestiture programme by Evergreen and Chancellor Broadcasting Co., which agreed to merge in February, to sell stations to meet FCC ownership limits. Since April 8, the companies have announced station sales totalling about $436 million.

The merged company, soon to be renamed Chancellor Broadcasting Co., will own and operate 96 stations in 21 of the nation's 40 largest markets. It will include 10 radio stations that Evergreen, based in Irving, Texas, has agreed to buy from Viacom International.
Evergreen's stock rose 31 cents to $39.44, while Chancellor Broadcasting gained 25 cents to $34.25 on Nasdaq in early afternoon trading.
